metadata.subject: CGM device market landscape and share analysis

footer.text: Competitive Intelligence Group — internal use only. Sourced from public filings, regulatory databases, and field interviews.

runs.text: Half-year update — June 2026. Coverage: US, EU5, Japan. Prepared for the Diabetes Care business unit leadership team.

elements.text: Summary of movement since the December 2025 edition

The CGM category grew to an estimated $15.8B in trailing-twelve-month global revenue, up 17% year-over-year, with over-the-counter (OTC) wellness wearers now contributing roughly 9% of category units. Three developments alter the competitive picture this half. First, Dexterra Health received FDA clearance for its 21-day G8 sensor in March, leapfrogging the category's wear-time benchmark of 15 days. Second, Verranova's OTC sensor Lumia crossed one million cumulative activations within nine months of launch, validating the cash-pay wellness segment it created. Third, Kizuna Medical's exit from its US distribution agreement with MedSource returns approximately 4% of US pharmacy share to contest during H2 2026.

Pricing pressure is concentrated in the type 2 basal segment, where payers increasingly benchmark against Verranova's $89/month cash price. Average US net revenue per patient-month declined an estimated 6% over the trailing year across the big three, while sensor cost curves improved faster (Dexterra disclosed a 14% unit-cost reduction at its March analyst day), keeping gross margins broadly stable.

elements.text: Dexterra Health — category leader, widening its clinical moat

Dexterra converted its March clearance of the 21-day G8 sensor into immediate formulary leverage: it has already renegotiated two of the three largest US PBM contracts to a per-patient-month structure that neutralizes per-sensor price comparisons. Manufacturing scale-up in Penang is tracking to a 40% capacity increase by Q1 2027. The G8 launch cadence (US March, Germany and UK June, Japan filing submitted May) is the fastest multi-region rollout in the company's history.

items.text: Strengths: longest wear time on market (21 days); deepest AID-pump integration ecosystem (four pump partners); direct-to-watch transmission cleared in US and EU.
Vulnerabilities: no OTC offering and management has signaled none before 2027, ceding the wellness segment; G8 adhesive complaints trending 2.1x G7 baseline on MAUDE, a potential quality narrative.
Watch items: pediatric label expansion decision expected Q4 2026; rumored acquisition interest in a closed-loop algorithm startup.

elements.text: Abelard Diabetes Care — volume leader defending the value segment

Abelard remains the unit-volume leader (an estimated 6.4 million active wearers) on the strength of its low-cost Libra 4 platform and unmatched pharmacy distribution. Its response to Dexterra's wear-time lead is a dual-analyte glucose-ketone sensor, submitted to FDA in April 2026 — a differentiation play rather than a wear-time race. The company's basal type 2 coverage wins in France and Japan added an estimated 380,000 covered lives this half.

items.text: Strengths: lowest manufactured cost per sensor in the category; 78 country registrations; strongest type 2 and OTC-adjacent brand equity.
Vulnerabilities: accuracy (MARD 8.9%) now trails Dexterra and Meridian; app ratings declined after the February firmware recall (1.2M sensors, no injuries reported).
Watch items: dual-analyte FDA decision expected H1 2027; German reimbursement renegotiation opens September 2026.

elements.text: Meridian Biosensors — implantable niche seeking scale

Meridian's 180-day implantable Everon system continues to own the long-duration niche, and its May 2026 CE mark for fully non-adjunctive dosing removes its last labeling disadvantage in Europe. Growth is constrained by the insertion-procedure model: field interviews indicate average wait times of five weeks for insertion appointments in US metro areas. The company signed a co-promotion agreement with two large endocrinology networks to expand insertion capacity.

items.text: Strengths: only 180-day sensor; strongest reported patient retention (86% at 12 months); premium net pricing.
Vulnerabilities: procedure bottleneck caps addressable volume; no pediatric indication; single-source chemistry supplier.
Watch items: 365-day sensor pivotal trial fully enrolled, data expected Q2 2027.

elements.text: Verranova — the OTC disruptor moving upmarket

Verranova's Lumia remains the fastest-growing product in the category from its cash-pay wellness base, and the company is now moving deliberately toward medical positioning: it initiated a type 2 non-insulin outcomes study (n=2,400) in May and hired a veteran market-access team from the pump industry. Its subscription model (89% of buyers on auto-renew) produces retention economics the reimbursed players cannot see in their own channel data.

items.text: Strengths: category-defining consumer brand and app engagement (41% DAU/MAU); direct subscription economics; influencer-driven acquisition cost under $70 per activated wearer.
Vulnerabilities: no reimbursed revenue; accuracy positioned for wellness (MARD 10.4%); churn concentrated at month 4 when novelty fades.
Watch items: outcomes study readout 2027; potential FDA enforcement attention on glucose-adjacent wellness claims industry-wide.

elements.text: Specifications as publicly labeled or disclosed at 30 June 2026. MARD figures are from each manufacturer's pivotal study and are not head-to-head comparable.

Reading the matrix: wear time and price are the visible battlegrounds, but the AID pump-partner column is the stickiness story — a wearer on a closed-loop system faces a device-ecosystem switch, not a sensor switch. Dexterra's four-partner position is the strongest structural lock-in in the category.

For our Diabetes Care unit, the half's developments sharpen three strategic questions: whether to accelerate our own extended-wear program, how to respond to cash-pay price anchoring in basal type 2, and whether the Kizuna US distribution vacancy is worth contesting.

items.text: Extended wear: reprioritize the 18-day sensor variant for a Q3 2027 filing; the 21-day benchmark will be table stakes in payer negotiations by 2028. Estimated incremental program cost $22M.
Cash-pay defense: pilot a $95/month direct subscription in two US regions in Q4 2026, fenced to non-insulin users, to blunt Verranova's anchor without disturbing reimbursed net pricing.
Kizuna vacancy: pursue the MedSource pharmacy slots opportunistically but cap trade investment at $8M; the share is low-margin and loyal to rebate depth rather than platform.
Quality narrative: commission an independent adhesive-tolerability study now; if Dexterra's G8 complaint trend persists, we want peer-reviewed comparative data in market by mid-2027.

runs.text: Revenue and share estimates triangulate company filings, IQVIA pharmacy panel data, import records, and 34 field interviews conducted April-June 2026 with endocrinologists, DME distributors, and payer pharmacy directors in the US, Germany, and Japan. Figures for private companies (Verranova) are estimates with a ±15% confidence band. This document contains no material non-public information; sourcing register available on request.
